The two-hand practice
There is a simple and easy body technique to connect with your inner child. Just place one hand in the center of your chest, which physically connects you to your love, and then place your other hand just below that, on your solar plexus, where your inner child can be.
Imagine a divine Love from above, with the inner child below, in the solar plexus area.

You can also use the hand on the solar plexus to massage that area.
Begin to send love from your heart down to your inner child and just notice what comes up for you. If some comes back up, let it, and send it on down again, so it goes around like a loop.
That part's a gift from them, and they don't owe it to you, so if nothing comes back, just keep sending yours.
If you feel resistance, just meet it with love.
If you feel or see something, just meet that with love as well.

If you can't find any warmth today, don't fake it, just leave your hands where they are and notice what's there.
Keep breathing gently the whole way through.
The Sober induction below lists this practice as one of its anchors, so it works as an induction too.

windows: The personal accounts and the way I arrange this practice are my own, especially adaptations like combining body-oriented work and hypnotic work.

This combination is not a scientifically validated form of treatment at this time. The Cochrane Collaboration has not yet awarded me their highest medal of honor.
Learning, entering, and returning
Healing the Divided Self, Maggie Phillips and Claire Frederick (1995), pp 24-27, 45-50, 83-90, covers a lot of aspects of this post, such as interactive hypnosis, helping the subject learn how to learn by using other senses, learning self hypnosis, making sure the subject comes back at the end, etc. However, this is a professional clinical book, not a self help book, so be careful about trying to use the procedures used with the cases, etc in this book for solo work (and the same goes for its historical claims). Also, Adam Eason and Benjamin Parris's article about self hypnosis for the International Society of Hypnosis should be a useful thing to read (especially the parts that talk about how to learn to learn when you're directing it yourself, and about whether you need another person to help you, and using recordings to help you, etc.)
Indirect language and re-entry cues
For information about using indirect hypnotic language patterns, such as pacing, utilizing, metaphor, and associational cues, etc, see Healing the Divided Self, Phillips and Frederick, 1995, pp 53-57, 96-100, as well as Nimja's tutorial on hypnotic language patterns, and his tutorial on triggers (he didn't write or endorse this guide, by the way).
They're where these techniques come from, but they're not on the hook for every NLP claim I make, or for whether every example suits trauma work.
I adapted the language for my own purposes, and I deliberately used a sequence that would be easy to use for re-entry.
